title: Introduction to Authentication
overview: Authentication is the process of verifying the identity of a user before allowing access to an application.

example.title: Authentication Flow
example.content:
User Login
 ↓
Verify Credentials
 ↓
Allow Access

title: Authentication vs Authorization
overview: Authentication verifies who the user is, while authorization determines what actions the user can perform.

example.title: Difference
example.content:
Authentication:
Who are you?

Authorization:
What can you access?

title: Password Hashing
overview: Passwords should never be stored as plain text. Hashing converts passwords into secure encrypted values.

example.title: Hashing Example
example.content:
Password
 ↓
Hash Algorithm
 ↓
Stored Hash Value

title: JWT Authentication
overview: JSON Web Token (JWT) is a popular method for securely transmitting user information between client and server.

example.title: JWT Flow
example.content:
Login
 ↓
Generate Token
 ↓
Send Token
 ↓
Verify Token

title: Protecting Routes
overview: Protected routes allow access only to authenticated users by verifying tokens or user sessions.

example.title: Protected Route
example.content:
Request
 ↓
Check Token
 ↓
Allow / Reject Access

title: Role Based Authorization
overview: Role-based authorization controls access based on user roles such as admin, user, or moderator.

example.title: Roles Example
example.content:
Admin → Manage Users
User → View Data
Moderator → Manage Content

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned authentication, authorization, password security, JWT tokens, protected routes, and role-based access control.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ Authentication verifies identity.
✔ Authorization controls permissions.
✔ JWT secures API access.
✔ Roles define user permissions.
